transcript: Yesterday, Paul and I went to see Doubt on Broadway, knowing little to nothing about the plot but leaving very impressed. Set at a Catholic school in the Bronx in the 60s, the school principal has suspicions about the priest and will stop at nothing to get to the bottom of them. It’s a story about certainty and uncertainty and the dangers of both of them. This production is a tight 90 minutes and the entire cast is stellar. It’s tense, the dialogue is sharp and intentional, and as an audience member you're left to grapple with your own doubts. Throughout the play, It’s hard to tell who's right and what to believe, and I think that makes it a really great play and a very engaging experience. Along with Purlie Victorious and Appropriate, this definitely contributes to the list of great play revivals so far this season. With that, another playbill for my collection.
